#Module frames

Nested browsing contexts for JavaScript (src/page/frames.odin, frames_scripts.odin, frames_access.odin; native/js/odin/frames.odin). A window of another document is named by its navigable's id: each document runs in its own engine instance, so another window is a WindowProxy of the calling realm. Across origins it reaches what HTML lets a cross-origin window reach (postMessage, location as a setter, closed, frames, length, top, parent, opener, window, self, close, focus, blur). The windows a script opens (window.open, links to _blank) are top-level navigables of the same kind (src/page/auxiliary.odin). Between documents of one origin, nodes are reached directly: every node handle names its document (base.pool_insert_tagged), the browser routes the call to it and checks the origin on each call.

Exposed to: Window. Source: api/frames.widl.

#Frame_bridge

u32 Frame_bridge(u64 realm, bytes request)

A request of the value bridge (native/js/odin/frames_bridge.odin) to another realm: the size of its reply, read with Frame_bridgeReply; 0 when that realm is gone or may not be reached.

Host: Frame_bridge :: proc(c: ^Call, realm: u64, request: []u8) -> u32

#Frame_bridgeReply

bytes Frame_bridgeReply()

The reply of the last Frame_bridge.

Host: Frame_bridgeReply :: proc(c: ^Call) -> []u8

#Frame_adoptNode

bytes Frame_adoptNode(u64 node, u64 into) raises

Moves node, of another document, to the document holding into (DOM "adopt"), as lone nodes: the handles of the nodes moved, each old one (u64) followed by its new one (the first pair is node's). Security when one of the two cannot be reached.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_adoptNode :: proc(c: ^Call, node: u64, into: u64) -> ([]u8, Api_Error)

#Frame_postMessage

void Frame_postMessage(u64 navigable, bytes data, usvstring target_origin) raises

otherWindow.postMessage(message, targetOrigin): data is the message's structured serialization (runtime/clone.c); target_origin is "*", "/" or a URL. The message is delivered from a task of the target's, if its document's origin then matches. Syntax for an invalid target origin, Data_Clone for a message over frames.max_message_bytes.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_postMessage :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, data: []u8, target_origin: string) -> Api_Error

#Frame_navigate

void Frame_navigate(u64 navigable, usvstring url, bool replace) raises

otherWindow.location = url, location.href = url, location.replace(url): Security when the calling document may not navigate it (HTML "allowed to navigate", the sandbox; the console says why), Syntax for an invalid URL.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_navigate :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, url: string, replace: bool) -> Api_Error

#Frame_open

u64 Frame_open(usvstring url, string target, string features) raises

window.open(url, target, features): _self, _parent, _top, or the name of a frame or of a window of the calling document's browsing context group is navigated and its navigable returned; _blank or a name nothing has opens a new window (when the embedder can: src/page/auxiliary.odin) whose opener is the calling document, and gives its navigable. 0 when nothing was opened, and under the features noopener / noreferrer. Syntax for an invalid URL.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_open :: proc(c: ^Call, url: string, target: string, features: string) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#Frame_opener

u64 Frame_opener(u64 navigable)

window.opener: the navigable whose document opened this top-level one; 0 for a frame, a window opened with noopener, one whose opener relationship ended (Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy, opener = null), or once the opener is gone.

Host: Frame_opener :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64) -> u64

#Frame_close

void Frame_close(u64 navigable)

window.close(): a window a script opened is closed (closed is true at once; its embedder closes it in a task). Any other window stays open (the console says why).

Host: Frame_close :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64)

#Frame_disown

void Frame_disown()

window.opener = null: the calling document's window has no opener any more.

Host: Frame_disown :: proc(c: ^Call)

#Frame_postMessagePorts

void Frame_postMessagePorts(u64 navigable, bytes data, usvstring target_origin, u64[] ports) raises

otherWindow.postMessage(message, targetOrigin, [ports]): the same, with the MessagePorts of the transfer list shipped as port ends (Port_ship / Port_entangle): the receiver's MessageEvent.ports are bound to them.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: Frame_postMessagePorts :: proc(c: ^Call, navigable: u64, data: []u8, target_origin: string, ports: []u64) -> Api_Error

Host: Window_get_name :: proc(c: ^Call) -> string
